subject: Carve-out approach + stepwise upgrade proposal for Clearline
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Carve-out approach + stepwise upgrade proposal for Clearline

Hi Elena —

Great to speak this morning. As promised, attaching a concise proposal that gives Clearline a path to move from the current Starter tier to a Multi-region Dedicated plan in two steps so you can preserve cost predictability while enabling the higher-throughput features you requested (batching pools, KV caching, and private VPC).

High level:
- Phase 1 (60 days): Upgrade to Compact Dedicated with a feature carve-out — add session pinning and prefix caching but hold off on multi-region routing. This minimizes churn and gives a ~12% unit-cost improvement.
- Phase 2 (after successful pilot): Full Dedicated Multi-region with autoscaling pool and SLA — targeted for Q1. Phase 2 includes an onboarding credit and a one-time configuration service.

Key asks for you:
1) Confirm you can pilot Phase 1 for 60 days (we'll track latency and cost per token).
2) Procurement: can your team sign the standard pilot SOW and accept the timeline below?
3) Any hard constraints for proration or billing windows we should be aware of?

I've included an appendix with pricing math and two options for discounting: a 10% pilot discount or a 15% pilot discount if Clearline commits to Phase 2 within 45 days of Phase 1 start. If procurement needs different language, flag it and we'll loop legal.

Attachments: CL-Proposal_stepwise-20261214.pdf (proposal), redlines_clearline_jonas_v1.docx (suggested contract redlines).

Next steps: I'd love to get a short confirmation by EOD Wednesday and can book a 20-min handoff meeting between your procurement and our pricing ops to finalize the SOW.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Elena Rossi <elena@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearlinehealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 12:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Carve-out approach + stepwise upgrade proposal for Clearline

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions before we loop procurement and legal: 

1) Proration: we run monthly billing cycles. If Phase 1 starts mid-cycle, will you prorate to our month boundary or invoice from the calendar start? We need predictable month-over-month numbers.

2) Pilot discount: the 15% conditional discount sounds attractive. Can you confirm that the discount applies to committed throughput (the reserved pool) only and not to overage charges?

3) SLOs: For Phase 1, what latency percentile do you commit to (p50/p95) and is that different in Phase 2? We'll need the language for procurement.

4) Redlines: Procurement attached a short list of redlines (separately). Does the redline doc you attached reflect typical language changes or are there any commercial items inside it we should focus on?

We're roughly ok with the timeline but need to keep the launch window flexible by a week depending on security review.

If you can reply with those specifics, I'll move procurement to a tentative sign-off.

—Elena
Director, Platform Partnerships | Clearline Health
elena@clearlinehealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Carve-out approach + stepwise upgrade proposal for Clearline

Elena — thanks, good questions. Short answers below and a compact table in the attached PDF.

1) Proration: We will prorate to your monthly billing boundary if you provide the billing cycle start date in the SOW. Our default is calendar-month, but we can align to customer cycle for pilot billing.

2) Discount applicability: Correct — the pilot discount applies only to the committed reserved capacity (the Compact Dedicated pool). Overage usage (on-demand) will be billed at standard overage rates. We'll highlight that in the SOW.

3) SLOs: Phase 1 (Compact Dedicated): p50 <= 20ms, p95 <= 120ms under expected pilot load (details in appendix). Phase 2 (Multi-region Dedicated): p50 <= 12ms, p95 <= 85ms with SLA and escalation playbooks. Those numbers are in the proposal and procurement SLO exhibit we can include in the contract.

4) Redlines: The redlines doc is mainly legal clarifications and one commercial ask around 30-day termination rights for the pilot. We flagged it as negotiable. No change requested to pricing formulas except the conditional discount option.

For procurement: if you want to proceed with the 15% conditional discount, we'll need an internal approval from RevOps for that concession (I copied Marissa to speed it up). Could procurement share the pilot start window so we can tentatively slot capacity?

If helpful, I can join procurement's meeting tomorrow at 10am ET.

Best,
Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Carve-out approach + stepwise upgrade proposal for Clearline

Looping in from RevOps — quick note: we've reviewed the proposal and approve a 15% pilot discount on the committed Compact Dedicated pool provided Clearline signs Phase 2 commitment language (non-binding milestone to commit to Phase 2 within 45 days of Phase 1 kickoff) and agrees to the proration alignment Jonas outlined.

A couple of operational clarifications for procurement:
- The 15% pilot discount will be applied as an invoice credit on the first monthly invoice after Phase 1 billing completes.
- Overages will not be discounted; they will appear as separate line items.
- We will include the SLO exhibit for Phase 1 as a non-SLA operational target and reserve the SLA enforcement for Phase 2 (full Dedicated SLA).

Jonas — please share the final SOW (billing-cycle date included) and the updated redlines doc for procurement signature. Elena — please let us know the intended pilot window and whether procurement prefers DocuSign or emailed countersign.

Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
